A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same null-model cheating study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena-Hard-Auto, and MT-Bench, plus open-source judge experiments and defense analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds attack comparisons, structural ablations, defense tests, additional judges, and transfer experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed structured-response attack and Universal Random Search remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 only renames the prefix variable; the lower-complexity responses are experimental ablations of the retained construction.

E1.justification: The benchmark datasets and UltraFeedback instruction source remain unchanged. Coverage expands within AlpacaEval 2.0 to direct cross-judge transfer and perturbed-response scenarios, including defenses applied to clean GPT-4o responses (Appendices C.2 and C.4).

E2.justification: Table 7 adds evaluated NullModel adaptations of Chen et al. (2024c), Raina et al. (2024), and Shi et al. (2024). Table 8 adds Self-Reminder and SmoothLLM defense comparisons. Table 3 removes the CoT-GPT-4-Turbo and GPT-4-Turbo reference comparator rows.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces substantial additional evaluation procedures: reminders in system and user messages, SmoothLLM insert/swap/patch perturbations, a perturbation-rate sweep, clean-response controls, and direct GPT-4-to-GPT-3.5 attack transfer. Mistral and SOLAR judge configurations are also added. The original experiments' stated sample counts and search budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds response-complexity ablations, defense sensitivity and clean-response degradation analyses, cross-judge transfer testing, and an instruction-following versus attack-susceptibility comparison (Tables 7–10 and Figures 18–21). These substantially extend v1's existing position, random-search, template-paraphrasing, and perplexity analyses.

E5.justification: The existing Arena-Hard-Auto 95% confidence intervals and boxplot reporting are retained. v2 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run information, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2's headline results remain unchanged. New results include 99.9% and 95.3% LC win rates against Mistral and SOLAR, 62.5% under Self-Reminder, and GPT-3.5 transfer rates of 13.5% for Structured and 0.4% for Structured+RS. Tables 7–10 and Figures 18–21 add substantial condition-specific findings; Table 3 removes two comparator result rows.

T1.justification: The formal judge definitions, threat assumptions, and algorithmic reasoning are retained, with no added theorems or proofs. Prefix-variable renaming and correcting existing plot labels to negative log probability do not introduce substantive theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim that constant, irrelevant outputs can obtain top benchmark scores without access to test instructions. The headline scores, proof-of-concept framing, and call for anti-cheating mechanisms remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 3–4 revise the default-position mechanism from last-output preference to preference for the first counterfeit output, with expanded explanations in Figures 2 and 9. Appendix C adds substantive interpretations about structural complexity, defense effectiveness versus clean-response damage, and poor transfer across judges.

D1.justification: v2 documents the NLTK vocabulary used by the word-level baseline, replacement of GCG with random search, the exact Self-Reminder text and placement, additional model checkpoint links, and simplified response templates. The original algorithm, hardware disclosure, and project-code link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. on evaluator bias, Robey et al. on SmoothLLM, and Xie et al. on Self-Reminder. The relocated related-work discussion changes the citation for input-specific attacks from Raina to Shi. The broader novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 condenses main-text related work while preserving the fuller discussion in Appendix A, separates the conclusion, places existing limitations under a new ethics statement, and makes localized explanatory and cross-reference corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–10 and Figures 16–21. It moves v1 Figure 8 into the main text as Figure 2 with an expanded caption, revises attack-component coloring and mechanism captions, corrects negative-log axis labels, and rearranges several existing displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence supporting and bounding the vulnerability: v1 lacked the explicit prior-attack comparisons, structural-complexity controls, and defense-versus-clean-response tests now provided in Appendix C. Reporting failed cross-judge transfer also makes applicability limits clearer. The comparisons use adapted baselines and uncertainty reporting remains limited, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical scrutiny.
